posts.card_line: The human is the point, not the asterisk.
posts.text:
Every AI roadmap sells the same future: you, edited out of the loop as a favor to efficiency.

A future told as inevitable is usually a future someone is selling.

There's a second road. The machine sharpens you instead of replacing you. I call it notomation.

The tell for which road you're on is smaller than you think. A 2026 study found AI web writing carries a structural fingerprint, detected at 97% (macro-F1) from structure alone, and still 96% after the text is reworded by the model that wrote it. Polish doesn't fix it. Only a human actually thinking does.

New essay: linkedin.com/pulse/notomation-zach-harris-4yjce

posts.title: Slop is the tell
slides: Slop is the tell. How to see which road your AI tools are putting you on.
Automation removes the human to save the step. Notomation keeps the human and removes the fog.
The tell is small. When a model writes for you and you fix its tics, you become its proofreader.
Each edit is tiny. You start writing a little more like the tool, so its drafts need less fixing.
A 2026 study, SlopShape, found AI web writing has a structural fingerprint: detected at 97% (macro-F1) from structure alone.
Reworded by the model that wrote it, detection barely moved: 96%. Polish does not remove the shape.
The shape changes only when a human actually thinks. The tell and the cure are the same act.
Make the tool bend to your register. Not the reverse.
posts.text:
Slop isn't just ugly writing. It's the visible residue of a person recalibrating to the machine, one small edit at a time.

The fingerprint survives rewording. The only fix is a human actually thinking.

posts.card_line: Optimist or pessimist is a weather report. It is not a compass.
posts.text:
52% of US adults are more concerned than excited about AI (Pew, 2026). That's the room's temperature, not the fork. The fork is whether AI compounds what's yours or you dissolve into it.

linkedin.com/pulse/notomation-zach-harris-4yjce

#Notomation #HumanIsThePoint

Atomize your skill into reusable pieces. Spread it. Grow it into the next thing.

Those are the verbs on both roads of the AI future.

On one road, AI compounds what's yours: your judgment gets sharper and more portable, and you carry it anywhere.

On the other, the same verbs quietly dissolve you into the tool. Your skill becomes its training data, and you become its proofreader.

Same verbs. Opposite polarity. That's the whole fork.

The question worth asking every week: am I using AI to compound what is mine, or am I dissolving into it?
